body:
WHAT
The engine and its frontends talk over a line-based JSON wire protocol defined in engine/protocol/src/types.ts (CoreEvent = engine-to-frontend events, FrontendRequest = frontend-to-engine requests, PROTOCOL_VERSION). The TUI keeps its own hand-written copy of the subset it uses in tui/src/protocol.ts. Nothing generates or checks that copy, so this record demands that its version number and every event and request type it declares agree with the engine's definitions.

WHY
The wire contract is the seam the repo calls most dangerous; a field renamed or a type dropped on the engine side would compile fine in the TUI and only fail at runtime by silently ignoring or misreading frames.

WHERE
tui/src/protocol.ts — PROTOCOL_VERSION, TaskItem, Usage, Question/QuestionOption, SessionSummary, SlashCommandInfo, PermissionDecision, RestoredMessage/RestoredToolCall, union types CoreEvent and FrontendRequest (with a loose catch-all arm for file_edited | addon_draft | addon_export); engine/protocol/src/types.ts — PROTOCOL_VERSION, CoreEvent, FrontendRequest, Frame and the same named interfaces; runtime version check: tui/src/engine/useEngine.ts session_started handler comparing event.v to PROTOCOL_VERSION.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. PROTOCOL_VERSION exported from tui/src/protocol.ts equals PROTOCOL_VERSION exported from engine/protocol/src/types.ts (import both at test time or parse the constant literals).
2. Parse both files with the TypeScript compiler API: every string literal in the TUI CoreEvent union's `type` discriminants (session_started, turn_started, tool_output_delta, retry_status, text_delta, thinking_delta, tool_call_started, tool_call_finished, agent_spawned, agent_finished, permission_request, question_request, task_list_updated, addons_updated, overdrive_changed, command_output, context_update, session_report, session_list, turn_finished, error, session_restored, model_catalog, cwd_changed, background_notification, file_edited, addon_draft, addon_export) also appears as a `type` discriminant in the engine's CoreEvent union.
3. Every `type` discriminant in the TUI FrontendRequest union (user_message, steer_message, permission_response, question_response, interrupt, set_overdrive, set_model, slash_command, bang_command, list_sessions, resume_session) appears in the engine FrontendRequest union with the same required property names and compatible types.
4. For each event arm the TUI declares with fields, every property name it reads (e.g. cwd_changed.worktree, permission_request.subject/grant, agent_spawned.background, session_started.commands, turn_finished.usage) exists on the corresponding engine arm, and a property required in the TUI copy is not optional in the engine copy.
5. A type-level assignability check compiles: `const e: TuiCoreEvent = engineEvent` fails only for the documented catch-all arm, i.e. assigning engine.CoreEvent to the TUI CoreEvent (and TUI FrontendRequest to engine FrontendRequest) typechecks with tsc --noEmit.
